title: Postpartum haemorrhage (PPH): first response and escalation
subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
setting: Labour room, operating theatre, postnatal ward, emergency department
summary: Measure blood loss objectively and act at 300 mL with an abnormal vital sign or at 500 mL. Start the whole first-response bundle within 15 minutes: uterine massage, IV oxytocin, tranexamic acid 1 g within 3 hours of birth, IV crystalloid, genital tract examination and escalation.

sections.title: Recognise and diagnose
items: Measure blood loss objectively at every birth (calibrated under-buttock drape at vaginal birth). Visual estimation consistently underestimates loss.

WHO 2025 trigger for treatment: measured loss of 300 mL or more with any abnormal haemodynamic sign (pulse above 100/min, systolic BP below 100 mmHg, diastolic BP below 60 mmHg, or shock index above 1), or loss of 500 mL or more, whichever comes first, within 24 hours of birth.
Be most vigilant in the first 2 hours after birth, but keep checking for revealed or concealed bleeding for 24 hours. Palpate uterine tone routinely in every woman.
Severe PPH is 1000 mL or more. Shock signs appear late in young women; anaemic women (common in India) decompensate after smaller losses.

Think of the 4 Ts: Tone (atony), Trauma (tears, haematoma, uterine rupture or inversion), Tissue (retained placenta or membranes), Thrombin (coagulopathy from abruption, pre-eclampsia or HELLP, amniotic fluid embolism, sepsis).

sections.title: First-response bundle (start all within 15 minutes)
items: Call for help (senior obstetrician, anaesthetist, midwife). Two large-bore IV cannulae; send group and crossmatch, CBC, coagulation screen and fibrinogen. Empty the bladder with a catheter.
Massage: rub the uterine fundus through the abdomen until it is firm and bleeding slows; repeat or continue intermittently as needed.

Oxytocin: 10 IU IV, diluted and given slowly over 1 to 2 minutes (or in a small crystalloid volume over 5 to 10 minutes), even if prophylactic oxytocin was already given. Then 10 to 20 IU in crystalloid over the next 4 hours, titrated to uterine tone.

Tranexamic acid: 1 g IV over 10 minutes as soon as PPH is diagnosed and within 3 hours of birth, whatever the cause (atony or trauma). Give a second 1 g if bleeding continues after 30 minutes or restarts within 24 hours. Do not start it more than 3 hours after birth.
IV fluids: warmed isotonic crystalloid (Ringer lactate or 0.9% saline) in preference to colloids; reassess after each bolus and avoid overload, especially in pre-eclampsia or heart disease.
Examine: check the placenta and membranes for completeness and inspect the vagina, cervix and perineum for tears and haematoma; repair bleeding tears promptly.
Escalate if bleeding continues despite the bundle: senior obstetrician, theatre, blood bank, or immediate transfer to a facility that can operate and transfuse.
India: the 2015 MoHFW PPH guidance reserves tranexamic acid for bleeding not controlled by uterotonics. This protocol follows WHO 2025, which gives it to every woman with PPH within 3 hours of birth.

sections.title: Second-line uterotonics
items: If IV oxytocin is unavailable or bleeding does not respond, WHO 2025 recommends IV ergometrine, oxytocin-ergometrine fixed-dose combination, or a prostaglandin including sublingual misoprostol 800 mcg. No sequence is proven; choose by availability and contraindications.
Methylergometrine 0.2 mg IM or slow IV. Do not use in hypertension, pre-eclampsia or heart disease.
Carboprost (15-methyl prostaglandin F2 alpha) 250 mcg deep IM, repeated every 15 minutes if needed, maximum 8 doses (2 mg). Avoid in asthma.
Misoprostol 800 mcg sublingual once. Adding misoprostol to oxytocin already given for treatment brings no extra benefit; expect shivering and fever.
Carbetocin given as prophylaxis should not be repeated for treatment (not adequately studied).

sections.title: Refractory bleeding: mechanical and surgical
items: Temporising measures while definitive care is arranged: bimanual uterine compression, external aortic compression, non-pneumatic anti-shock garment.

Uterine balloon tamponade for atony after vaginal birth that does not respond to first-line treatment, only where surgery and blood are available, retained tissue and trauma are reasonably excluded, and the woman can be closely monitored.
Do not pack the uterus with plain or haemostatic gauze.

Continuing bleeding: laparotomy with compression (brace) sutures, uterine or internal iliac artery ligation, or hysterectomy; uterine artery embolisation where available and the woman is stable enough.

Retained placenta with PPH: give a uterotonic and proceed to manual removal under anaesthesia, with a single prophylactic antibiotic dose (ampicillin or a first-generation cephalosporin, or amoxicillin 1 g plus clavulanic acid 200 mg IV).

sections.title: Blood products (WHO 2025 targets)
items: Decide on transfusion from the clinical picture and ongoing loss, not a single haemoglobin; early Hb is falsely reassuring. Activate the massive transfusion protocol for ongoing loss of 1000 mL or more with unstable vital signs.
Red cells: crossmatched if time allows, group-specific if not, O RhD-negative in an emergency. Therapeutic goal usually Hb above 7 g/dL.

Fibrinogen: keep 2 g/L or more; this usually needs 3 to 4 g of fibrinogen (about 8 to 10 units of cryoprecipitate). Prioritise fibrinogen over FFP when coagulopathy is suspected (abruption, amniotic fluid embolism).
FFP: if coagulation results are not yet available after 4 units of red cells, give 1 unit FFP for every 2 units of red cells; target PT and APTT below 1.5 times control and INR 1.5 or less.

Platelets: transfuse 5 to 10 mL/kg when there is microvascular bleeding and the count is below 50 x 10^9/L. Whole blood (crossmatched or low-titre group O) may be used where components are unavailable.

sections.title: After bleeding is controlled
items: Pulse, BP, respiratory rate, SpO2, uterine tone and vaginal loss every 15 minutes initially, then at reducing intervals for 24 hours; hourly urine output via catheter and a strict fluid balance chart.
Repeat CBC and coagulation tests; look for concealed bleeding (vulval or broad ligament haematoma, intra-abdominal bleeding after caesarean).
Start pharmacological thromboprophylaxis once bleeding has stopped and coagulopathy is corrected.
Treat postpartum anaemia: oral iron for 6 to 12 weeks, or IV iron when oral iron is not tolerated or severe anaemia needs rapid correction. Debrief the woman and family before discharge.

sections.title: Prevention at every birth
items: Give one uterotonic in the third stage for all births: oxytocin 10 IU IM or IV (IV diluted and given slowly over 1 to 2 minutes when a line is already in place).
Where the oxytocin cold chain is unreliable use heat-stable carbetocin 100 mcg IM or IV; if neither is available, misoprostol 400 or 600 mcg orally.
Do not use ergometrine, oxytocin-ergometrine, carboprost or tranexamic acid for routine prevention at vaginal or caesarean birth.

Identify risk antenatally (previous PPH, placenta praevia or accreta spectrum, multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios, anaemia, prolonged labour) and plan birth where blood and surgery are available; correct anaemia before term.
Controlled cord traction by skilled attendants; do not clamp the cord before 1 minute unless the baby needs resuscitation.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting for 500 mL, hypotension or a falling Hb before acting, or relying on visual estimation.
Giving bundle components one after another instead of together, and missing the 3-hour tranexamic acid window.
Methylergometrine in pre-eclampsia or hypertension; carboprost in asthma.
Assuming atony when the uterus is firm: look for trauma, retained tissue, uterine inversion or a concealed haematoma.
Repeated crystalloid boluses without reassessment, causing dilutional coagulopathy and pulmonary oedema.

drugs.name: Oxytocin
drugs.dose: Treatment: 10 IU IV diluted, slowly over 1 to 2 minutes, then 10 to 20 IU in crystalloid over 4 hours titrated to tone. Prevention: 10 IU IM or slow IV
drugs.notes: First-line for prevention and treatment. Repeat dosing is safe after prophylaxis. Avoid rapid undiluted IV push (hypotension).

drugs.name: Tranexamic acid
drugs.dose: 1 g IV over 10 minutes; second 1 g if bleeding continues after 30 minutes or restarts within 24 hours
drugs.notes: Start within 3 hours of birth for every PPH. Not for routine prevention. Avoid with a known thromboembolic event in this pregnancy.

drugs.name: Methylergometrine
drugs.dose: 0.2 mg IM or slow IV; may repeat after 15 minutes, then every 2 to 4 hours if needed; maximum 5 doses (1 mg in total)
drugs.notes: Contraindicated in hypertension, pre-eclampsia and heart disease.

drugs.name: Carboprost (15-methyl PGF2 alpha)
drugs.dose: 250 mcg deep IM every 15 minutes as needed; maximum 8 doses (2 mg)
drugs.notes: Avoid in asthma. Diarrhoea, vomiting, fever and bronchospasm are common.

drugs.name: Misoprostol
drugs.dose: Treatment: 800 mcg sublingual once. Prevention: 400 or 600 mcg orally once
drugs.notes: Use when injectable uterotonics are unavailable. Shivering and pyrexia common.

drugs.name: Carbetocin (heat-stable)
drugs.dose: 100 mcg IM or IV once, for prevention only
drugs.notes: Alternative to oxytocin where the cold chain cannot be guaranteed. Not for treatment after prophylactic carbetocin.
